p1.title: Passage 1
paras: The New Education Policy (NEP) introduced in India seeks to reform the traditional education structure by emphasizing flexibility, multidisciplinary learning, and skill development. Unlike earlier systems that largely prioritized rote memorization and examination performance, the NEP advocates conceptual understanding, creativity, and critical thinking. The policy also proposes integrating vocational education and digital technology into mainstream learning. Supporters argue that such reforms can better prepare students for the demands of a rapidly changing global economy. However, critics contend that implementation remains a major challenge, especially in rural and economically disadvantaged regions where infrastructure, trained faculty, and digital access are limited. Concerns have also been expressed regarding linguistic diversity and the practical feasibility of certain policy recommendations. Despite these debates, many educational experts consider the NEP one of the most ambitious reforms attempted in recent decades. Its long-term success will ultimately depend on effective administration, teacher preparedness, and equitable access to educational resources.

p2.title: Passage 2
paras: Financial behavior among youngsters has undergone considerable transformation in the digital era. Easy access to online banking, digital wallets, instant credit systems, and e-commerce platforms has made financial transactions more convenient than ever before. However, financial experts argue that such convenience has also encouraged impulsive spending and weakened the traditional culture of savings among young people. Many adolescents and young professionals increasingly associate financial success with visible consumption rather than disciplined wealth management. Social media platforms further intensify this trend by promoting luxury lifestyles and instant gratification. Economists warn that inadequate financial literacy at an early age can lead to long-term debt dependency and poor investment decisions. Consequently, educational institutions and financial organizations have begun introducing programs on budgeting, saving, taxation, and responsible borrowing. Advocates of financial education believe that cultivating saving habits during youth not only improves individual economic security but also contributes to broader economic stability within society.

questions.q: Identify the error: “Each of the nurses have been given a new uniform.”
questions.why: 'Each of' takes a singular verb: 'has been given'. GPSC-style practice item, modelled on the 2026 grammar blocks.

questions.q: Choose the correct conditional sentence:
opts: If he left earlier, he would have caught the train.
If he would have left earlier, he would have caught the train.
If he had left earlier, he would have caught the train.
If he had left earlier, he would catch the train yesterday.
questions.why: Third conditional: if + past perfect, would have + past participle. Never 'would have' in the if-clause. GPSC-style practice item, modelled on the 2026 grammar blocks.

questions.q: Spot the error: “Either the clerk or the officers is responsible for the delay.”
questions.why: With either/or, the verb agrees with the nearer subject ('officers'): 'are'. GPSC-style practice item, modelled on the 2026 grammar blocks.

questions.q: Identify the error: “I am knowing the new doctor since last year.”
questions.why: 'Know' is a stative verb, and 'since' needs the present perfect: 'I have known'. GPSC-style practice item, modelled on the 2026 grammar blocks.

questions.q: Choose the correct option: “I wish I ______ the answer to your question.”
questions.why: 'Wish' about the present takes the past form (subjunctive). GPSC-style practice item, modelled on the 2026 grammar blocks.

questions.q: Find the next number in the series: 7, 10, 16, 28, 52, ?
questions.why: The differences double each time: 3, 6, 12, 24, then 48. So 52 + 48 = 100.

questions.q: Each letter is given its position in the alphabet (A = 1, B = 2, and so on) and a word's value is the sum of its letters, so GOA = 7 + 15 + 1 = 23. What is the value of PANAJI?
A man walks 4 km south, turns left and walks 3 km, then turns left again and walks 8 km. How far and in which direction is he from his starting point?
questions.why: He ends 3 km east and 4 km north of the start. The straight-line distance is 5 km, to the north-east.

questions.q: One morning just after sunrise, Vikram stood facing a pole. The shadow of the pole fell exactly to his right. Which direction was he facing?
questions.why: After sunrise shadows fall to the west. If west is to his right, he is facing south.

questions.q: The average age of 30 students is 15 years. Including the teacher, the average rises by 1. What is the teacher's age?
In a certain code PEN is written as QGQ. How is INK written in that code?
questions.why: The letters move forward by 1, 2 and 3 places: I-J, N-P, K-N.

questions.q: In a certain code each letter is replaced by the letter in the same position counted from the other end of the alphabet, so GOA becomes TLZ. How is INDIA written?
questions.why: I-R, N-M, D-W, I-R, A-Z.

questions.q: If '+' means multiply, 'x' means subtract, '-' means divide and '/' means add, what is the value of 8 + 6 x 12 - 4 / 5?
questions.why: After substitution: 8 x 6 - 12 / 4 + 5 = 48 - 3 + 5 = 50.

questions.q: In a certain language 'sun rises east' is written 'pa ko ti', 'east or west' is written 'ti la mu' and 'sun sets west' is written 'pa ru la'. Which word means 'rises'?
questions.why: 'pa' is sun (first and third phrases) and 'ti' is east (first and second), so the remaining word 'ko' is rises.

questions.q: Find the next letter in the series: Z, X, U, Q, L, ?
questions.why: The steps back are 2, 3, 4, 5, then 6. L is the 12th letter, so the next is the 6th, F.

questions.q: According to §9, in the healthy condition the material organism is governed by:
questions.why: Topic 1, Organon and Philosophy. §9: in health the spirit-like vital force (dynamis) rules with unbounded sway and keeps all parts in harmonious operation.

questions.q: According to §7, the totality of symptoms is:
opts: the outwardly reflected image of the inner essence of the disease
questions.why: Topic 1, Organon and Philosophy. §7: the totality must be the principal, indeed the only, thing the physician has to take note of in every case.

questions.q: According to §16, the vital force can be affected only by:
questions.why: Topic 1, Organon and Philosophy. §16: being spirit-like, it can be deranged and restored only by dynamic influences.

questions.q: Who compiled 'The Guiding Symptoms of our Materia Medica'?
questions.why: Constantine Hering's Guiding Symptoms runs to ten volumes. Kent wrote the Lectures on Homoeopathic Materia Medica, Boericke the Pocket Manual and Allen the Keynotes.

questions.q: A patient who feels his body is enormously enlarged and time passes too slowly, with exaltation and uncontrollable laughter, needs:
questions.why: Topic 2, Materia Medica. Cannabis indica: errors of time and space, exaltation.

questions.q: Constant hunger with a 'better while eating' state, emaciation despite eating well, and enlarged hard glands suggest:
questions.why: Topic 2, Materia Medica. Iodium: hungry, hot, restless and emaciated; hyperthyroid picture.

questions.q: Sour-smelling diarrhoea with green, frothy stools like the scum of a frog pond, in milk-intolerant infants, suggests:
questions.why: Topic 2, Materia Medica. Magnesia carb: sourness of the whole body.

questions.q: The remedy Lachesis is prepared from:
opts: the venom of the bushmaster snake
questions.why: Topic 3, Pharmacy. Lachesis muta, the South American bushmaster.

questions.q: Remedies such as X-ray, Magnetis polus and Sol are drawn from which source?
questions.why: Topic 3, Pharmacy. Imponderabilia are 'weightless' energies: X-ray, magnetism, sunlight, electricity.

questions.q: Boenninghausen's Therapeutic Pocket Book (1846) is divided into how many sections?
questions.why: Mind, parts of body, sensations, sleep and dreams, fever, modalities (alterations of the state of health) and relationship of remedies.

questions.q: In Kent's Repertory, a desire for salt is found in the chapter:
questions.why: Topic 4, Repertory. Food desires and aversions are rubrics under Stomach in Kent.

questions.q: The hallmark of irreversible cell injury is:
opts: Nuclear changes such as karyolysis and pyknosis
questions.why: Swelling and fatty change are reversible.

questions.q: Reed–Sternberg cells are characteristic of:
questions.why: Topic 6, Pathology, Microbiology and Diagnostics. Large binucleate 'owl's eye' cells, CD15 and CD30 positive.

questions.q: A generalised tonic-clonic seizure lasting more than 5 minutes is treated as:

questions.q: Lower abdominal pain, fever, purulent vaginal discharge and cervical motion tenderness suggest:
